Supplier Management
A cross country pipeline is a long-distance pipeline system designed to transport fluids—such as crude oil, natural gas, water, or chemicals—across vast geographic areas. These pipelines typically run over varied terrains including deserts, hills, rivers, and populated regions, connecting production sites with refineries, processing facilities, storage terminals, or distribution centers. We specialize in the design, installation, and commissioning of cross-country pipeline systems for oil, gas, water, and industrial applications. Our turnkey solutions ensure reliable product transportation over long distances, across deserts, mountains, and urban zones.
Cross Country Pipeline
Engineering & Design
Comprehensive pipeline engineering and route design solutions, incorporating terrain analysis, stress modeling, and compliance with international codes and client specifications.
Steel Pipes of All Sizes
Supply and installation of carbon steel pipes in various diameters and thicknesses to suit oil, gas, and water transmission applications.
3LPE, Insulation, FBE Coated Pipelines
Pipelines coated with 3-Layer Polyethylene (3LPE), insulation jackets, and Fusion Bonded Epoxy (FBE) to ensure corrosion resistance and thermal protection in harsh environments.
Road/Water/Mountain Crossings
Execution of complex crossings under roads, rivers, and mountains using trenchless technologies like HDD, boring, and microtunneling, ensuring minimal surface disruption.
Dewatering / Sheet Piling
Groundwater control through dewatering and structural soil support using sheet piling for safe excavation and trench stability in water-logged or loose soil conditions.
Control Cables / Cathodic Protection
Installation of control cables for monitoring systems and cathodic protection systems to prevent corrosion and extend the service life of buried pipelines.
De-magnetization
Application of pipeline degaussing (de-magnetization) to neutralize magnetic fields that can interfere with welding quality or pipeline operation.
Long Radius Cold Bends
Fabrication and installation of long-radius bends using cold bending techniques to maintain flow efficiency and reduce the number of welded joints.
Hot Tapping & Pigging
Live pipeline connections through hot tapping without shutdowns and internal cleaning/inspection using pigging systems to maintain flow integrity.
Vaporizer / Liquid Nitrogen Purging
Use of liquid nitrogen and vaporizers for inerting and purging pipelines to ensure safe working conditions during repairs or commissioning.
Cold Cutting
Precise, spark-free cutting of pipes using cold cutting techniques—ideal for hazardous environments where fire or heat must be avoided.
Automatic Welding
High-quality, consistent welds achieved through automatic and semi-automatic welding systems, improving speed, productivity, and safety in pipeline fabrication.
Tekzone is among the leading cross-country pipeline contractors in the UAE, managing end-to-end pipeline installations for oil factories pipeline contractors. We handle various terrains with advanced coatings and protective measures, ensuring durable and safe pipelines for oil, gas, and other industries.

Oil & Gas Pipelines
KEC launched its Oil and Gas Pipelines EPC business in line with the Government’s thrust in the sector and our strategy to diversify the business portfolio into adjacencies. The business focuses on the construction of Oil & Gas / Slurry pipelines and Composite Mechanical, Civil, Electrical and Instrumentation work in Hydrocarbon Facilities in India as well as in international markets.
In the past year, KEC Spur Infrastructure Private Limited (formerly known as Spur Infrastructure Private Limited) achieved an annual turnover of INR ~480 and possesses a profitable track record. The Company has successfully completed major projects for large Indian PSUs which include Indian Oil Corporation Limited’s (IOCL) 12” x 200 kms Mainline, HDD and Composite Works for Patna-Siwan & Siwan-Motihari of the Patna-Motihari-Baitalpur (PMBPL) project and 16" x 126 Kms Tundla - Gansara Cross Country Product Pipeline.
Some major ongoing projects of KEC Spur are:
JSW Utkal - Laying of Iron Ore Slurry Pipeline from Jajpur to Paradip - 32" X 129 Kms

Additionally, KEC Spur Infrastructure is also executing City Gas Distribution projects for IGL/Torrent Gas & Think Gas.

HVDC submarine cable electrification project in Abu Dhabi
HVDC submarine cable electrification project in Abu Dhabi
Offshore Energy
A joint Venture of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), Electricité de France (EDF) and Kyushu Electric Power Japan has awarded a HVDC cable installation and convertors package for the ADNOC-TAQA Lightning Project to a consortium composed of Jan De Nul Group and Samsung C&T. Jan De Nul will be in charge of the design, installation, burial and protection of two cable clusters of almost 1,000 km in total, connecting the islands Al Ghallan and Das in the Arabian Gulf to the onshore converter stations at Al Mirfa and Shuweihat in Abu Dhabi (UAE).
The two cable links are part of the larger Subsea Transmission System (Lightning Project) of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) and the Abu Dhabi National Energy Company (TAQA), and will connect Abu Dhabi’s onshore electricity grid to all ADNOC’s offshore production facilities.
The first cable cluster, connecting Das Island to shore, comprises three 400 kV subsea cables of 135 km each. The second cluster, connecting Al Ghallan island to shore, concerns four 320 kV submarine cables of 125 km each. The commissioning of the project is scheduled for 2025.
First subsea installation project of its kind in the Middle East
The package awarded to Jan De Nul and Samsung is currently the first-of-its-kind HVDC submarine cable project in the Middle East and MENA region. The consortium’s contract value is 3 billion USD of which 725 million USD for Jan De Nul’s scope. “This electrification project is the biggest cable installation contract in the history of Jan De Nul. This project will entail many of Jan De Nul’s versatile expertises such as cable laying, dredging, jet-trenching, rock protection, landfall preparation, riser platform fabrication and offshore installation. With two of the world’s largest cable installation vessels in our fleet (the Isaac Newton and the Connector), we are well prepared for the future works in the DC and AC subsea cable markets”, says Wim Dhont, Manager Offshore Cables.
Decarbonization to support ‘Net Zero by 2050’ targets
With this strategic project, ADNOC and TAQA plan to significantly decarbonize ADNOC’s offshore production operations. Both parties have joined forces to support the United Arab Emirates in their net-zero targets.
The Lightning Project will replace the existing offshore turbine generators with cleaner and more sustainable onshore power sources from Abu Dhabi, such as solar panels and local nuclear power. This will reduce the carbon footprint of ADNOC’s offshore facilities by more than 30 per cent.

DEWA Awards 21 Contracts Worth AED 3 Billion for 132kV Substations and Transmission Cable Projects in Dubai
July 24, 2026
Mohammad S
Power
Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) has awarded 21 contracts valued at approximately AED 3 billion for the construction of 132kV transmission substations and associated underground transmission cable networks across several key areas of Dubai.
The contracts form part of DEWA’s ongoing investment in strategic electricity transmission infrastructure to meet the emirate’s growing power demand and support residential, commercial, and economic development projects.
The awarded contracts cover the construction of 132kV transmission substations in several districts, including Al Barsha South Fourth and Fifth, Al Jaddaf, Al Yalayis First, Al Yufrah First, Bu Kadra, Jebel Ali First, Airport City, Me’aisem First and Second, Saih Al Dahal, Umm Suqeim First, Wadi Al Safa Third, Warsan Second and Fourth, and Zabeel Second.
Advertisement
In addition to the substation construction works, DEWA has awarded contracts for the installation and extension of approximately 64 kilometres of 132kV underground transmission cables to connect the new substations to the main electricity transmission network.
The AED 3 billion contract package represents a major expansion of Dubai’s high-voltage electricity transmission infrastructure and will strengthen the reliability and capacity of the emirate’s power network.
Separately, DEWA Managing Director and CEO HE Saeed Mohammed Al Tayer announced that the authority’s strategic investments in electricity transmission network projects have now exceeded AED 10 billion.
During the first half of 2026, DEWA commissioned eight 132kV substations with a combined transformation capacity of 1,200 MVA, at a total cost of AED 970 million. The projects also included the installation of approximately 20 kilometres of transmission cables.
DEWA also commissioned a 400/132kV transmission substation at Saih Al Dahal, located within the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Solar Park. The substation has a total transformation capacity of 2,000 MVA and was developed at a cost of AED 630 million. The project scope also included the construction of approximately 117 kilometres of 400kV overhead transmission lines.
Looking ahead, DEWA is currently developing 65 new 132kV substations and one 400kV substation in collaboration with its main contractors and suppliers. Over the next three years, the authority plans to issue tenders for more than 30 additional 132kV substations, alongside the installation of approximately 340 kilometres of underground transmission cables and the construction of two additional 400kV substations.
The newly commissioned 132kV substations include facilities serving Madinat Hind 4, Al Khairan First, Al Layan First, Nad Al Sheba First, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Gardens, Al Barsha South Fourth, Me’aisem Second, and Al Manara, supporting electricity demand from major residential and development projects across Dubai.
As of the end of the first half of 2026, DEWA’s transmission network comprised 402 transmission substations, including 28 substations at 400kV level and 374 substations at 132kV level.
According to DEWA, the strategic transmission projects are being developed to enhance the efficiency, reliability, and resilience of Dubai’s electricity network while supporting the emirate’s continued economic and urban growth. The projects also align with the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33 and Dubai Social Agenda 33.
The latest investments demonstrate DEWA’s continued focus on expanding high-voltage transmission infrastructure and ensuring sufficient electricity capacity to meet current and future demand across Dubai.

Despite the announcement, KPIL shares traded lower on the NSE, declining 1.14 per cent to ₹1,375.30 as of 09.55 am, against a previous close of ₹1,391.20Kalpataru Projects International Limited (KPIL) on Monday announced it has received a Letter of Award (LoA) for the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) of a gas pipeline project in the United Arab Emirates, classified as a “Major” order, indicating an estimated contract value exceeding ₹4,000 crore.The Mumbai-based EPC company disclosed the win to BSE and NSE through a regulatory filing dated September 28, 2026, noting the order was received in the normal course of business. No further details on the client, project timeline, or precise contract value were disclosed.Despite the announcement, KPIL shares traded lower on the NSE, declining 1.14 per cent to ₹1,375.30 as of 09.55 am, against a previous close of ₹1,391.20. The stock had opened higher at ₹1,420 and touched an intraday high of ₹1,424.80 before sellers dominated, with 58.16 per cent of traded quantity on the sell side. Total traded value stood at ₹8.28 crore in early trade. The company’s total market capitalisation was ₹23,460.73 crore.MD & CEO Manish Mohnot called the win a testament to the company’s technical expertise and global scalability in the oil and gas sector.KPIL reported revenues of ₹27,143 crore in FY2026 and currently has over 250 projects under execution across 30-plus countries, with a global footprint spanning 75 nations.Published on September 28, 2026 THIS AD SUPPORTS OUR JOURNALISM.
